prose: An Ask HN on a gap many agent users feel: the poster finds chatgpt.com's top-tier model consistently more insightful than Codex's agent models, but with far weaker tool calling - so they shuttle context between the two by hand and want that intelligence living in their local agent instead. The early answers sketch the community's workarounds: build specialised subagents that tease out more thinking from reasoning-budget-limited models (one commenter details the approach while flagging it as unproven), effectively using orchestration to buy back the intelligence the agent harness leaves on the table.
highlights: Ask HN: how to get the most intelligence out of your agents
Poster: chatgpt.com's top tier outsmarts Codex agents but can't call tools
Current workaround: manually copying context between the two
Community suggestion: specialised subagents to extract more reasoning from budget-limited models
The intelligence-vs-tool-use trade-off between chat and agent surfaces remains unsolved
